topic: The Hidden Geometry of Counting: From Ternary Systems to Fractals
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

outline.topic: The Hidden Geometry of Counting: From Ternary Systems to Fractals
outline.target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Mathematics majors)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Ternary Foundation
sections.content: Introduce base-3 counting (0, 1, 2) as a language of 'choice' rather than 'quantity'. Use a branching tree diagram to show how 3 bits represent 27 states (3^3), setting the stage for 3-peg logic.
sections.example: A smart lock with 3 buttons (A, B, C) where each press changes the state; show how 3 buttons represent positions in a 3-dimensional coordinate system.

sections.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
sections.content: Explain the variation where disks can only move between adjacent pegs (A↔B, B↔C). Connect the movement to the ternary system: each disk state transition requires a specific base-3 increment. Visualize this as a path on a line.
sections.example: Representing the state of 3 disks as a 3-digit ternary number (e.g., 000 to 222), where each valid move adds 1 in 'ternary arithmetic'.

sections.title: Mapping the Sierpinski Triangle
sections.content: Transition from the 1D path of Hanoi moves to a 2D graph. Demonstrate that the sequence of allowed moves in the constrained Hanoi problem perfectly traces the edges of a Sierpinski triangle. Use an animation showing the path 'growing' as more disks are added.
sections.example: A spider crawling between three anchor points; as it visits every possible sub-triangle, its path recreates the Sierpinski fractal pattern.

sections.title: Synthesis: The Deep Connection
sections.content: Conclude by unifying the concepts: The Sierpinski graph represents the state-space of the constrained Towers of Hanoi, and ternary numbers serve as the 'GPS coordinates' to locate any point within that fractal structure.
sections.example: A visual overlay: showing a ternary coordinate (1, 0, 2) and highlighting the exact corresponding vertex within a 3rd-order Sierpinski triangle.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Ternary Foundation
lecture_lines: Ternary systems use three digits: zero, one, two.
They represent choices, not just simple quantities.
Three bits create twenty-seven distinct states.
Think of buttons defining a coordinate system.
This structure builds our foundation for logic.

storyboard.title: The Constrained Towers of Hanoi
lecture_lines: Disks move only between adjacent pegs.
State transitions follow ternary arithmetic increments.
Each move adds one to the state.
The sequence maps linearly on a path.
This constrains the Tower of Hanoi.
animations: Display 3 pegs with disks in color #F1FAEE.
Move disk 1 to middle peg using rule.
Move disk 2 to end peg with animation #A8DADC.

storyboard.title: Mapping the Sierpinski Triangle
lecture_lines: Now, map these moves to two dimensions.
The path traces a Sierpinski triangle.
Each disk expansion grows the fractal.
Anchor points guide the pattern's evolution.
The entire graph reveals the geometry.
animations: Draw a large triangle in color #457B9D.

storyboard.title: Synthesis: The Deep Connection
lecture_lines: Ternary numbers are our fractal GPS.
They locate vertices within the structure.
The graph represents the total state-space.
Logic and geometry unify perfectly here.
This concludes our hidden geometry exploration.
animations: Overlay Hanoi disk pattern onto Sierpinski vertices.
Fade between Hanoi path and Sierpinski structure.
